what: Lid camera stills after @timothy-commins backed the knurled back-focus ring all the way out ("extended the adapter all the way"), 2026-10-23
stills: still_1904Z_ring_all_the_way_out.jpg (after the Pi's scheduled 13:00 MDT reboot at 19:00:22 UTC; unchanged, mean |difference| 1.5 grey levels)
saved_at: half resolution (2028 x 1520); measured at full resolution
how: ssh to the lid camera Pi over the tailnet, then curl -s localhost:8081/still (picam_source.py); the stream kept running
ot2: rail lights already on (GET /robot/lights); no maintenance run and no current protocol run; nothing on the robot changed

focus_score.note: still at the exposure and gain limits (66.7 ms, gain 15.5-16), so the score is mostly noise; don't read focus from it

scale.method: dark well centres (local minima), median nearest-neighbour spacing over ~280 links; 9 mm plate pitch
scale.reading: the picture is a third bigger: moving the lens further from the sensor magnifies it. With the 12.5-22.4 mm ring travel (9.9 mm), that puts the exit pupil about 30 mm in front of the sensor at 18:08, if the zoom wasn't touched

blur.reading: about half the blur of 18:08; the wells' rims and the gaps between wells now show, but it is not sharp (a sharp still would have a spot of a few px)

focus_side.method: focus_side.py: each paint-filled well fitted as a disc convolved with a triangular blur spot, apex up or down, or a round spot (focus_side.json)
focus_side.18:08: apex up in 4/4 wells, by 12-83 % in rms: the iris's upright shape, picture behind the sensor (calibration: ring fully in, focus at NEAR)
focus_side.18:54_and_19:04: apex down in 8/8 wells, but only by 0.2-6 % in rms: leaning towards the turned-over shape, picture in front of the sensor
focus_side.plausibility: If the spot had NOT turned over, halving it with a 9.9 mm move would leave about 10 mm still to add (delta2 = 9.9 / (137/70 - 1)), about 15 mm past the 17.53 mm C-mount flange distance; at 25-35 mm zoom that focuses 0.07-0.12 m away, not on a plate 0.6 m away, which a lens rated 0.2 m to infinity at 17.53 mm can't need. If it HAS turned over, the picture is about 9.9 / (1 + 137/70) = 3.3 mm in front of the sensor, and the right ring position is about 6.6 mm out from fully in: 1.6 mm past the C-mount distance, inside the 1.1-2.2 mm (f^2/(u-f)) that a 25-35 mm zoom needs for 0.6 m with focus at FAR. The thin-lens fit of the scale change agrees only with the turned-over reading and has the focus near FAR.
caveats: the 9.9 mm assumes the ring went from fully in to fully out
the 18:08 and 18:54 spot sizes assume the iris and zoom weren't changed in between
the up/down margin today is small; the at-the-robot test in the README settles it

advice: Don't stack another spacer on the ring as it is now. Nudge the focus thumbscrew: sharper towards FAR (or blurrier towards NEAR) means the lens is too far from the sensor, so back the knurled ring in about 3 mm (deck-to-silver-rim gap about 22-23 mm by Tim's 16 mm reference), then refocus from FAR. A 5 mm C-CS ring is still worth having so the knurled ring can sit 1-2 mm out from fully in, mid-thread, instead of at the end of its travel.
